cells.tense: You are moving through this without needing to see where it ends, and the step you take is the whole story for now.
cells.ask: Take the next step on the thing you're unsure about, then tell one person what you did and what it cost you.
cells.core:
You can move through this without seeing where it ends. Enough light for the next step, not the whole route, and you've stopped fighting that. What you're carrying is heavy and you're carrying it cleanly, without bracing against the dark and without pretending to see farther than you can.

The step you take is small and real. That's the shape of it. You don't need more clarity than you have, and you don't need anyone to tell you you're doing it right. Keep the size of the step honest, and when the result lands, let the people who benefit from it know what it cost. The balance holds while you keep telling the truth about what you gave up to get here.
cells.sheetLine: You walk a road you can't see to the end, and the step is enough.
cells.verb: Stepping forward on partial light while the full route stays hidden.
cells.place: At the edge of what's known, where the next step shows and the rest doesn't.

cells.tense: You are already at a future where it's acknowledged, and you're rehearsing how you'll be received before anyone has received it.
cells.ask: Name the outcome you're bracing for, out loud, then do one small piece of the actual work today without telling anyone.
cells.core:
You're running ahead of where you actually are. The acknowledgment hasn't arrived yet, but you're already living in the version where it has. You rehearse the words, count who'll notice, shape the thing so it lands right. The shaping has started to replace the doing.

There's a cost to that. You're spending today on a tomorrow that may not come the way you've written it, and the work gets thinner the more you design how it will be greeted. You don't have to stop caring whether it's seen. Just stop rehearsing the moment before it's happened. Let the work be small and unremarkable today, and let the acknowledgment be something you can't control.
cells.sheetLine: You're living in the recognition before the work is done.
cells.verb: Stepping forward on partial light while the full route stays hidden.
cells.place: At the edge of what's known, where the next step shows and the rest doesn't.

cells.tense: You stood at a door where what you carried was going to be seen, and you're still standing there even though the door closed behind you.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you carried that nobody saw, keep the page, and start one small build you can still finish.
cells.core:
There was a place where what you gave was going to be seen, and it wasn't. Or it was, and something in you didn't arrive to meet it. You're still back there, at the moment before the acknowledgment, still holding the weight of a step that's already been taken. The road ahead has moved on without you.

What's gone isn't your ability to walk an unclear road. You can still do that. What's gone is your own standing on it. You're at the wrong part of the path, waiting for something that already happened or didn't. The way back is not to feel more or push harder into the hollow. It's to build one small thing with your hands, where the result will be visible and material, and let that carry you a step forward.
cells.sheetLine: You're still at the door where it was going to be seen.
cells.verb: Stepping forward on partial light while the full route stays hidden.
cells.place: At the edge of what's known, where the next step shows and the rest doesn't.

cells.tense: You are the one arranging how this gets understood, and you talk about it as if the shape were just there.
cells.ask: Pick something you've described as the situation and say, out loud, what you chose about it.
cells.core:
You set how this gets understood. You choose what gets said, what gets shown, how the story gets framed for whoever's going to hear it. But when you describe it, you talk like the shape was already there and you just found it. You made those calls and you keep making them. When you tell it, your hand doesn't show.

That's not dishonesty. It's a habit of leaving yourself out of the picture, especially when the picture includes something you gave up. Framing it one way rather than another is yours, and naming that doesn't make you vain. It makes the account true. You can still be modest about it. Just stop calling your own decision the situation's shape.
cells.sheetLine: You're shaping how this is understood and calling it just how it is.

attempts.check: Unsupported: that the person is 'held by community,' 'unseen,' or 'gave up something' — the record gives only the capacity and the status, never their history. The reader could object that nobody sacrificed anything or that recognition was never sought. The ask survives being wrong because it is an act of naming or attunement, not a claim about them. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'You're the one holding it open,' which flatters the reader by assigning a role the record does not name.
